title: Editor overlays applied by the runtimes
limitations: fusion_room_runtime applies the map editor's private room overlays (the private overrides/metroid/<area>_<NNN>.mvnative of the extracted assets, the editor's own save format read by the shared core/native_map reader) to the BG1 and BG2 block layers of every Zero Mission room it loads, at the start and through doors, when the document names the same room and tileset and has the room's layer dimensions; any other document is reported and ignored, and removing the file restores the reconstructed room. --no-overlays disables them and --overlay-dir DIR reads another directory. It also plays the room's project collision (the entities/<area>_<NNN>.json project document, schema metroidvania.project-room-data versions 2 to 4): each 16-pixel cell takes the smallest native Clipdata value of the native tables whose type and behavior are its type's counterpart (solid SOLID, one_way PASS_THROUGH_BOTTOM, hazard a lava air block, slope_up RIGHT_STEEP and slope_down LEFT_STEEP floor slopes, water a water air block, air AIR), without movement; a document of another room or other dimensions, with a cell outside, an unknown type or a type the tables cannot express is reported and ignored. The document's entities whose native reference is a Zero Mission sprite (PSPRITE_*) join every variant of the room's sprites at their 16-pixel block, with the variant's spriteset graphics slot for that sprite (else slot 0) and no room slot (0xFF); unassigned entities are skipped, and a document with an entity outside the room or a reference that is not a sprite is ignored. Its transitions to Zero Mission rooms lead their source door to the target's <area>_<NNN> export: a door adopted from a native door (native_source) redirects that native door, keeping its geometry and hatch, and any other door becomes a new hatchless door (index 1000 plus its id) whose blocks take the transition behavior of its facing (door for left and right, up and down transitions otherwise); Samus arrives with her feet at the spawn point, or without one (0, 0) beside the saved target door (one block past its inner edge, centred under an up door or over a down door), kept inside the target room; transitions to Aria are skipped, and a door off the block grid or outside the room or a transition with neither a spawn point nor a saved target door has the document's doors ignored. fusion_aria_runtime plays the project collision of its rooms (overrides/aria/entities/area_<AA>_room_<NNN>.json, 8-pixel cells, read by the same shared project_room_document loader): each cell replaces the native BG1 collision byte with its type's byte as the ported collision walks read it (solid 0x03, one_way 0x01 floor bit only, slope_up 0x45 the flipped 45-degree floor slope rising to the right, slope_down 0x41, air 0x00), at the start and on every room load except the transition audit, with the same --no-overlays and --overlay-dir DIR options; a document of another room or other dimensions, with a cell outside, an unknown type or a water or hazard cell (the runtime has no water or damage cells) is reported and ignored. The document's entities with an Aria native reference (<family>:<HH> of the editor's catalogue: enemy, special-object, generic-candle, pickup, hard-mode-pickup, all-souls-reward as kinds 1 to 6) join the room's entity records after the native ones, at the centre of their 16-pixel box (editor x and y plus 8), with no persistent index; a pickup's settings give var_a (its collection flag) from parameter_0, var_b (the item) from item_id and its flags, parameter_1 unused; the runtime plays the kinds and ids it has ported; unassigned entities are skipped and a document with an entity outside, an unknown reference or malformed item settings is ignored. Its transitions to Aria rooms are played: a door adopted from a native screen-edge transition (native_source variant transition-<edge>, native_type the index of its T entry) redirects that entry's target room and replaces its arrival by the spawn point, and any other door becomes a transition taken when Soma's body (his column and the 32 pixels above his feet) touches its 8-pixel rectangle, latched until he steps out of every editor door so an arrival inside one does not bounce; Soma's feet arrive at the spawn point or, without one, beside the saved target door, kept inside the target; transitions to Zero Mission are skipped, a target beyond the native 8-bit area or room ids is reported, and a door off the 8-pixel grid or outside the room, an adopted entry the room does not have or a transition without an arrival has the document's doors ignored. Checked on captures (edited blocks drawn; Samus falling through painted air and standing on painted solid cells; a placed Zoomer and Skree in Brinstar's save room; a new door in Brinstar's save room taking Samus to room 31 at its spawn point; native door 71 redirected to room 29, arriving beside the target project door, and room 31 again without overlays; in Aria's area 0 room 1, Soma stopped by a painted wall at x 151 instead of 199 and falling through a painted hole; a placed bat (enemy:00) and a Potion (pickup:02 item 0) appearing there, the Potion collected; a new door in that room taking Soma to room 2 at its spawn point; the right-edge entry redirected to room 5, and room 2 again without overlays). Limitations: native hatches and objects stay, an adopted native door keeps its native geometry, door_type (boss, locked, portal, save) has no effect, cross-world transitions are not played, and the editor's item settings and events have no engine adapter; a placed sprite outside its room's spriteset uses graphics slot 0 for its palette tricks; a painted cell drops the block's breakability and movement; Aria's runtime, which draws pre-composited room backgrounds, does not draw painted collision and applies no tile overlay, gives door types no effect, a pickup whose collection flag is above 191 never appears, and a pickup sharing a native pickup's flag counts as collected with it, and plays no water or hazard cell.

limitations: fusion_metroidvania runs both native title screens at once, separated by the source prototype's patch-0046 animated geometry: eight staggered Metroid bipolar triangles and eight staggered Aria Fermat spirals rotate clockwise at 10 degrees a second, without the later polarity mirror. X uses Zero Mission SOUND_RUINS_TEST_SHOOTING_LIGHTNING 0x1DC and Y uses Aria sound-table entry 0x081. Independent host-only per-player gains cross-fade native music player 0 while leaving SFX players audible at every divider angle; neither sequencer state nor native volume is changed. Holding either key for three seconds selects its existing runtime once through fusion_host, while releasing early cancels. The supplied JSON values are compiled defaults and --split-config accepts an optional strict JSON override. START retains the title-driven in-process launch flow. Limitations: startup sequences, idle introduction and demos remain deliberately skipped; the Aria menu-to-gameplay chain inside the launcher was not run in this cycle. Deterministic tests cover native-ID routing, separate player gains, geometry, JSON, hold and cancellation; headless captures cover composition. Sound choice is source-derived and locally waveform-reviewed, not emulator-compared. aos_mp2k_engine_load_bank now restores the 0xFF host player gains like init and set_bank (a shared engine_replace), so bank-loaded engines no longer mute every MP2K player; fusion_aos_mp2k_tests covers the defaults, per-player muting and a failed load, and fusion_sfx_browser --check now renders the Aria 0x081 and Zero Mission 0x1DC pulses offline and fails on silent PCM. Held X/Y pulses now climb one semitone per 0.5 s beat from six below the native pitch (saturating at +12) through host-only per-player pitch controls (aos_mp2k_player_pitch key_shift_public, mzm_audio_set_player_pitch in the native pitch routine); releasing the key resets the progression.
